notes: THE LOAD-BEARING CASE FOR THE CANCEL-CHECKOUT INVARIANT. After cancel_checkout, the USP booking resource as observed through GET /bookings/{booking_id} MUST NOT remain in a state from which Section 5.1.1 requires accepting confirm. The business's internal record is out of scope; this vector asserts the protocol surface only. canceled_at MUST be stable across reads, so a second get at a later timestamp returns the same value.

when.notes: Second read at a later instant. canceled_at MUST equal the value from the first get_booking.

wrong_answers.behaviour: leave the USP-visible booking pending after cancel_checkout
wrong_answers.why: Section 5.1.1 requires accepting confirm from pending, so the platform can confirm an unpaid booking. The record is also indistinguishable from a paid-awaiting-approval booking in manual confirmation mode, the booking-scoped credential is never invalidated, and the personal-data retention clock never fires.

wrong_answers.behaviour: return booking_status: pending on a checkout whose status is canceled
wrong_answers.why: Claims the checkout-scoped summary is still live while the checkout itself is terminal.

wrong_answers.behaviour: return the confirm refusal as a 4xx Problem Details response
wrong_answers.why: The request was understood and processed; invalid_transition is a business outcome carried at HTTP 200 in messages[], not a protocol error.

wrong_answers.behaviour: derive terminality from the absence of a live checkout session
wrong_answers.why: An implementation that cannot observe checkout-session lifetime cannot tell an in-flight checkout from a departed one, so it reports a booking whose buyer is mid-payment as canceled and then refuses that platform's own confirm.

wrong_answers.behaviour: stamp canceled_at with the current time on every read
wrong_answers.why: A later get_booking returns a different canceled_at, so platforms cannot treat the timestamp as the instant cancellation was recorded.

wrong_answers.behaviour: key the terminal state on USP pending rather than on the specific backing state the abandoned checkout left behind
wrong_answers.why: A business whose status mapping folds several backing states into USP pending will also match a manual-confirmation booking that is paid and awaiting merchant approval, which is pending under Section 7.5 derivation rule 1 and must never be reported canceled. Same failure for a booking that is paid after the platform walked away. The invariant applies to the booking the canceled checkout left unpaid, not to every booking reading pending.
